title: Localization of a relative Grothendieck fibration over a localized base
statement:
Use ordinary nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, equivalences and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent localizations of [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface], cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of small infinity categories with straightening classification of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], applied to opposites for cartesian fibrations; $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ is formed for the containing universe. All ordinary categories below are small in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck fibration of ordinary categories: for each $u:b\to c$ and $y\in\mathcal E_c$ there is an arrow $a:u^*y\to y$ over $u$ such that every arrow $z\to y$ over $u v$ factors uniquely through $a$ by an arrow over $v$. These are called cartesian lifts; no split cleavage is required. Let $U\subseteq\mathcal B$ and $W_b\subseteq\mathcal E_b$ be wide subcategories containing the isomorphisms. Suppose every pullback functor $u^*:\mathcal E_c\to\mathcal E_b$ preserves $W$, and for every $u\in U$ the induced functor
$$L(\mathcal E_c,W_c)\longrightarrow L(\mathcal E_b,W_b)$$
is an equivalence. Let $V\subseteq\mathcal E$ consist of arrows whose image is in $U$ and whose vertical factor, in a factorization as a vertical arrow followed by a cartesian lift, lies in $W_b$. This is independent of the cleavage. Replacing any of these marking classes by its saturation does not change its localization.

The localizations exist, and the induced arrow
$$L(\mathcal E,V)\longrightarrow L(\mathcal B,U)$$
is a cartesian fibration intrinsically, meaning equivalent as an arrow to a simplicial cartesian fibration. The canonical map from each fiber identifies $L(\mathcal E_b,W_b)$ with its infinity-categorical fiber over $b$. The localization map sends every ordinary cartesian lift to a cartesian edge, including lifts of base arrows outside $U$. Its classifying coherent functor under this straightening
$$L(\mathcal B,U)^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$$
sends $b$ to $L(\mathcal E_b,W_b)$ and $u$ to the functor induced by $u^*$. These identifications retain the natural transformations and all higher simplices of this family. A coherent functor out of $L(\mathcal E,V)$ is equivalently a coherent functor out of $N\mathcal E$ inverting $V$; if its target is a cartesian family over $L(\mathcal B,U)$, preservation of cartesian edges can be checked on the images of the ordinary cartesian lifts.
